question.knowledge_point: Finding the Domain and Asymptotes of a Transformed Function
question.problem: What is the domain of the function $f(x)=2\operatorname{sec}⁡(3x-{60}^{∘}),$ where $x$ is measured in degrees? Assume that $n$ is an integer.
question.worked_solution:
The domain of $y=\operatorname{sec}⁡x$ consists of all values where $\operatorname{cos}⁡x\ne 0,$ and is given by the expression

$$
x\ne {90}^{∘}+n\cdot {180}^{∘},
$$

where $n$ is an integer.

To find the domain of $2\operatorname{sec}⁡(3x-{60}^{∘}),$ we replace the $x$ on the left-hand side of the above with $(3x-{60}^{∘}).$ This gives

$$
3x-{60}^{∘}\ne {90}^{∘}+n\cdot {180}^{∘}.
$$

Solving for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3x-{60}^{∘} & \ne {90}^{∘}+n\cdot {180}^{∘} \\ 3x & \ne {90}^{∘}+n\cdot {180}^{∘}+{60}^{∘} \\ 3x & \ne {150}^{∘}+n\cdot {180}^{∘} \\ x & \ne {50}^{∘}+n\cdot {60}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the domain of the function is $x\ne {50}^{∘}+n\cdot {60}^{∘},$ where $n$ is an integer.
